ci_method: Callaway-Sant'Anna (2021) group-time ATTs aggregated with the 'simple' weighting (each ATT(g,t) weighted by its number of treated county-years), never-treated counties as the comparison group, universal base period; SE = 0.2104 from the multiplier bootstrap clustered at the county level (5,000 iterations, did::att_gt bstrap=TRUE, clustervars=county_id); CI = estimate +/- 1.96*SE. This interval reflects sampling uncertainty only and does NOT include uncertainty about the parallel-trends assumption, which is untestable for the cohort carrying 69% of the weight (see assumptions_checked).
specifications_run: Static two-way FE: new_biz_per_10k ~ program | county + year, cluster(county). Estimate -0.447 (SE 0.213, p=0.037). DISCARDED: with staggered adoption and effects that grow with exposure, TWFE puts large negative weights on long-exposed county-years; here the 2006 cohort (69% of treated county-years, treated in 15 of 16 years) acts as a 'control' for later adopters while its own effect is still growing, flipping the sign. Reported only as a diagnostic of the bias.

Dynamic TWFE event study: i(event_time, treated, ref=-1) | county + year, cluster(county). Pre-period coefficients flat (-0.39 to +0.06, all |t|<2.5); post coefficients rise monotonically from +0.92 at e=0 to +15.21 at e=14. Used as a diagnostic, not for the headline (still contaminated by already-treated comparisons).
PREFERRED: Callaway-Sant'Anna, control_group='nevertreated', base_period='universal', xformla=~1, aggte(type='simple'). ATT = 7.179 (SE 0.210), 95% CI [6.767, 7.592].
Callaway-Sant'Anna, control_group='notyettreated', aggte(type='simple'). ATT = 7.038 (SE 0.149). Agrees with the never-treated version.

Callaway-Sant'Anna dynamic (event-time) aggregation. Overall 8.199 (SE 0.193); ATT(e) = 1.04, 2.27, 3.33, 4.01, 5.20, 5.91, 7.11, 8.27, 9.23, 10.06, 11.26, 12.48, 12.99, 14.22, 15.61 for e=0..14. NOT the requested estimand (equal weight per event time over-weights long exposures); used to characterise dynamics.

Callaway-Sant'Anna group/cohort aggregation. 2006 cohort 8.296 (SE 0.260), 2011 cohort 5.401 (SE 0.260), 2016 cohort 3.028 (SE 0.280); overall 6.450. NOT the requested estimand (equal weight per cohort regardless of cohort size/exposure).

Sun-Abraham interaction-weighted estimator: feols(y ~ sunab(cohort, year) | county + year), summary(agg='att'), cluster(county). ATT = 7.179 (SE 0.188) - numerically identical to the preferred CS estimate.

Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess imputation (hand-coded): county+year FE fit on untreated observations only, counterfactual imputed for treated observations, ATT = mean residual over treated county-years. Estimate 4.853 but computed on only 995 of 3,185 treated county-years. DISCARDED: restricted to untreated observations, each 2006-cohort county has a single observation (2005), so its county FE is a singleton and all 146 counties / 2,190 treated county-years (69% of the estimand) are dropped. The 4.853 is an estimate for the 2011+2016 cohorts, not for the requested ATT.

TWFE with county-specific linear trends: y ~ program | county + year + county[year], cluster(county). Estimate 0.828 (SE 0.079). DISCARDED: the treatment effect here IS an approximately linear growth in the outcome (~1.0/yr), so unit-specific trends mechanically absorb the effect; additionally the 2006 cohort has one pre-period, so its trend is not identified from untreated data at all.

Stacked DiD with clean controls: one sub-experiment per cohort (cohort vs 26 never-treated), sub-experiment-specific county and year FE, cluster(county). Estimate 4.973 (SE 0.095). DISCARDED: the pooled regression's implicit weights across sub-experiments and event times do not match the requested county-year weighting (it effectively under-weights the long-exposure 2006 cohort); not an estimate of the target estimand.

Callaway-Sant'Anna with anticipation=1. ATT = 4.960 (SE 0.210). Not comparable: imposing one anticipation period makes the 2006 cohort 'already treated in the first period', so did drops all 146 of those counties; the number is an estimate for the 2011+2016 cohorts only.

Callaway-Sant'Anna dropping the 2006 cohort entirely (cohorts with testable pre-trends only). ATT = 4.721 (SE 0.203). Different estimand (mean exposure 3.8 vs 6.0 years); run as a robustness check on whether the untestable cohort drives the per-exposure-year pattern - it does not.
Leave-one-out jackknife: CS never-treated specification re-estimated 26 times, dropping one never-treated comparison county each time. ATT range [7.115, 7.265], sd 0.036.

Estimand verification: hand-computed average of the 30 estimated ATT(g,t) for t>=g, weighted by the number of county-years in each (g,t) cell = 7.1793, exactly matching did::aggte(type='simple') = 7.1793.
assumptions_checked: Data/design integrity: balanced panel verified (300 counties x 16 years = 4,800 rows, every county has 16 observations, no missing outcomes). 'program' is exactly consistent with 'adoption_year' (0 mismatches against the implied indicator year>=adoption_year). Treatment is absorbing: 0 counties ever switch the program off, so the staggered-adoption estimators apply. 3,185 treated county-years. Cohorts: 2006 (146 counties), 2011 (71), 2016 (57), never-treated (26).

Parallel trends, testable portion: 15 pre-treatment ATT(g,t) estimates are available for the 2011 and 2016 cohorts. All are small (max |ATT| = 0.571, most < 0.4) with no systematic pattern. Joint Wald test using the CS influence-function covariance: chi-sq = 0.039 on 15 df, p = 1.00. Cohort-specific pre-trend slopes (pre-period ATT regressed on event time): +0.049/yr for 2011 [-0.083, 0.181], +0.027/yr for 2016 [-0.018, 0.072], pooled +0.023/yr [-0.010, 0.055]. No detectable pre-trend.

Parallel trends, NON-testable portion (the main threat to this estimate): the 2006 cohort adopted in the second year of the panel, so it has exactly ONE pre-treatment year (2005), which is consumed as the base period. There are therefore ZERO pre-trend tests available for the 146 counties that supply 2,190 of 3,185 treated county-years (68.8% of the estimand) and all of the longest exposures. Each of those counties' fixed effects is pinned down by a single year of untreated data, so any 2005-specific shock or mean reversion in 2005 passes one-for-one into their estimated effect in all 15 post years. This is checked and explicitly NOT satisfied as a testable condition.

Internal-consistency check used in place of the missing 2006 pre-trends: regressing post-period ATT(g,t) on exposure within each cohort gives a dose-response slope of +0.999/yr for the 2006 cohort, +1.010/yr for 2011, and +1.002/yr for 2016, with intercepts of 1.30, 0.86 and 1.03. The cohort whose parallel-trends assumption cannot be tested reproduces, to within 1%, the exposure profile of the two cohorts whose pre-trends are testable and flat. A pre-existing differential trend in the 2006 cohort would have no reason to match the other cohorts' program dose-response this precisely.

Sensitivity to parallel-trends violation (hand-coded linear-trend sensitivity, HonestDiD-style; HonestDiD not installed): because the effect is averaged over a mean exposure+1 of 6.995 years, a differential linear trend of delta per year biases the ATT by about 6.995*delta. The break-even delta that would drive the ATT to zero is 1.026 per year. For scale, that is about 4x the never-treated group's own total outcome trend (0.267/yr) and roughly 20-45x the upper end of the measured pre-trend slopes. Bias-adjusted ATTs: delta=0.05 -> 6.83; delta=0.10 -> 6.48; delta=0.20 -> 5.78; delta=0.30 -> 5.08; delta=0.50 -> 3.68. The sign and statistical significance survive every plausible violation.

No anticipation: CS event-time estimates immediately before adoption are essentially zero (e=-1 is the normalised base, e=-2 is -0.154 (SE 0.245), e=-3 is -0.004). Re-estimating with anticipation=1 yields 4.960, but that specification mechanically drops the entire 2006 cohort, so it tests anticipation only for the 2011/2016 cohorts, where it is not detected.

Comparison-group choice and its thinness: never-treated controls give 7.179, not-yet-treated give 7.038 - the choice does not matter materially. However, only 26 counties are never treated, and from 2016 onward they are the ONLY available comparison group, so event times 10-14 (730 county-years, 23% of the estimand) rest entirely on those 26 counties. Leave-one-out jackknife over all 26 moves the ATT only within [7.115, 7.265] (sd 0.036), so no single control county drives the result, but the long-horizon estimates lean on a small and non-randomly-selected control pool.

Estimand alignment with the question asked: confirmed that the 'simple' CS aggregation is exactly the average of ATT(g,t) over treated county-years - the hand-computed county-year-weighted average of the 30 post-treatment ATT(g,t) equals 7.1793, matching aggte(type='simple') to four decimals. Cohort weights in that average are 68.8% / 22.3% / 8.9% for 2006 / 2011 / 2016.

Functional form / effect dynamics: the effect is NOT a level shift. It rises monotonically and almost exactly linearly from about +1.0 in the adoption year to about +15.6 after 14 years (~+1.0 per additional program year, R-sq of the linear fit > 0.99 within each cohort). The 7.18 figure is therefore an average over this exposure profile and is specific to the observed exposure mix (mean 6.0 years in program); it is not the effect of a county's first year in the program.

Inference: standard errors clustered at the county level (300 clusters) throughout; CS estimates use the multiplier bootstrap (5,000 iterations). Cluster count is comfortable for the overall estimate, though effective identifying variation for the longest horizons comes from 26 control counties.
headline_claim: Counties enrolled in the state small-business grant program recorded 7.2 more new business registrations per 10,000 residents per year than they would have absent the program (95% CI 6.8 to 7.6), averaged across all program county-years, with the gap widening by roughly one registration per 10,000 for each additional year a county stayed in.
